title: Lavoro e carriera
sub: Present perfect simple e continuous - il colloquio di lavoro
grammar: Present perfect simple vs continuous, for/since, how long

lessons.title: Da quanto tempo? Present perfect
lessons.intro: In un colloquio ti chiederanno «da quanto lavori lì?» e «che cosa hai fatto finora?». In italiano usiamo il presente («lavoro lì da tre anni»); in inglese serve il present perfect, semplice o continuous. Qui impari a scegliere con sicurezza.

steps.title: Present perfect simple: il risultato conta
steps.body:
Forma: **have / has + participio passato** (worked, written, been).

Si usa per collegare il passato al presente:
- **un risultato che vediamo adesso**: I've lost my keys. (e non li ho)
- **esperienze di vita, senza dire quando**: She has worked in three countries.
- **quantità** (how many / how much): I've sent twelve emails this morning.
- **situazioni che durano fino a oggi**, soprattutto con verbi di stato: I've known her for years.

Non si usa quando c'è un **tempo finito** (yesterday, last year, in 2019, ago): lì serve il past simple.
ex: I've applied for three jobs this month.
Questo mese ho fatto domanda per tre lavori.
He has been a teacher since 2012.
Fa l'insegnante dal 2012.

steps.title: Present perfect continuous: l'attività conta
steps.body:
Forma: **have / has + been + verbo in -ing**.

Si usa quando ti interessa **l'attività** e la sua **durata**, non il risultato:
- **un'azione iniziata nel passato e ancora in corso**: I've been working here for five years.
- **un'azione appena finita, con effetti visibili**: Your eyes are red. Have you been crying?
- **un'azione ripetuta di recente**: She's been going to the gym a lot lately.

È la forma naturale con **how long** quando parli di un'attività: How long have you been waiting?

**Verbi di stato** (know, like, have = possedere, be, believe, understand) **non** si usano al continuous: «I've been knowing him for years» è sbagliato -> I've known him for years.
ex: I've been learning English since I was twelve.
Studio inglese da quando avevo dodici anni.
It's been raining all day.
Ha piovuto tutto il giorno.

steps.title: Simple o continuous? Tre test pratici
steps.body:
1. **Quantità o durata?** Se dici quanto/quante volte -> simple. Se dici quanto tempo -> spesso continuous.
- I've written **three reports** today. / I've been writing **since nine**.
2. **Finito o in corso?** Il simple suggerisce che il lavoro è completo, il continuous che è (forse) ancora in corso.
- I've painted the kitchen. (è finita) / I've been painting the kitchen. (ci sto ancora lavorando, o ho appena smesso)
3. **Permanente o temporaneo?** Con live e work le due forme sono quasi uguali: I've lived / I've been living here for ten years. Il continuous dà un senso di situazione più recente o temporanea.

Il continuous non si usa con un **numero preciso di volte o oggetti**: «I've been writing three emails» è sbagliato.
ex: How many interviews have you had?
Quanti colloqui hai fatto?
How long have you been looking for a job?
Da quanto tempo cerchi lavoro?

steps.title: For, since, ago e how long
steps.body:
- **for** + periodo di tempo: for three years, for a long time, for ages.
- **since** + momento di inizio: since 2019, since Monday, since I left university (anche con una frase al past simple).
- **ago** + past simple: I left the company two years ago.
- **How long...?** chiede la durata: How long have you worked here?

**Errore tipico degli italiani**: «I work here since 2019» o «I'm working here from three years». In inglese, per una situazione che dura fino a oggi, serve il **present perfect**: I've worked here since 2019 / for three years.

Attenzione: se il lavoro è **finito**, si usa il past simple: How long **did** you work there? (non ci lavori più). How long **have** you worked there? (ci lavori ancora).
table: I've been here for two hours.
I've been here since ten o'clock.
ex: She's been a manager since she was thirty.
È responsabile da quando aveva trent'anni.
How long did you work in Berlin?
Quanto tempo hai lavorato a Berlino?

steps.s: She ___ for the same company since 2015.
steps.it: Lavora per la stessa azienda dal 2015.
steps.why: Situazione che dura fino a oggi con «since»: present perfect, non il presente come in italiano.

steps.s: Marco left the company two years ___ .
steps.why: «Ago» si mette dopo il periodo e vuole il past simple (left).

steps.s: My hands are covered in paint. I ___ the kitchen.
steps.why: Azione appena finita con effetti visibili: present perfect continuous.

steps.s: I ___ three reports today, and I haven't finished the fourth.
steps.why: Con un numero preciso di oggetti si usa il simple: have written.

steps.s: Come on, I ___ for you since eight o'clock!
steps.why: Azione in corso con «since»: present perfect continuous.

steps.q: Qual è la frase corretta?
steps.why: «Know» è un verbo di stato (niente -ing) e con «since» serve il present perfect.

steps.q: Quale domanda chiede da quanto tempo studi ancora inglese?
opts: How long have you been studying English?
How long are you studying English?
How long do you study English?
steps.why: Durata di un'attività che continua: have you been studying.

steps.q: Scrivi la forma giusta del verbo tra parentesi
steps.s: She ___ (work) here since she left university.
steps.why: Situazione che continua dal passato a oggi, con «since».

steps.q: Scrivi la forma giusta del verbo tra parentesi
steps.s: How long ___ (you / wait) for the bus?
steps.why: Domanda sulla durata con how long: present perfect, di solito continuous.

steps.q: Traduci in inglese
steps.text: Vivo a Torino da dieci anni.
answers: I've lived in Turin for ten years
I have lived in Turin for ten years
I've been living in Turin for ten years
I have been living in Turin for ten years
steps.why: In italiano si usa il presente; in inglese il present perfect con «for».

steps.q: Traduci in inglese
answers: How long have you been studying English
How long have you studied English
How long have you been learning English
How long have you learnt English
How long have you learned English
steps.why: Domanda con how long: present perfect (di solito continuous).

steps.s: I am working in this company since 2018.
answers: I have worked in this company since 2018
I have been working in this company since 2018
I've worked in this company since 2018
I've been working in this company since 2018
I have worked at this company since 2018
I have been working at this company since 2018
I've worked at this company since 2018
I've been working at this company since 2018
steps.why: Con «since» serve il present perfect, non il present continuous.

steps.s: She has been knowing him for years.
answers: She has known him for years
steps.why: «Know» è un verbo di stato: non ammette il continuous.

steps.s: I've been working here since three years.
answers: I've been working here for three years
I have been working here for three years
I've worked here for three years
I have worked here for three years
steps.why: «Since» vuole un momento preciso (2019, Monday); per un periodo si usa «for».
Inizio nel passato e situazione ancora attuale: present perfect + since.

steps.s1: It's two years since I last saw Maria.
steps.why: «It's two years since I last saw» = «non vedo da due anni»: haven't seen + for.

steps.s1: Her phone call started an hour ago and she is still talking.
steps.s2: She ___ the phone for an hour.
steps.why: Azione ancora in corso: present perfect continuous (oppure has been on the phone).

steps.it: Da quanto tempo lavori per questa azienda?
steps.en: How long have you been working for this company

lessons.title: Lavoro e carriera
lessons.intro: Il lessico per parlare di candidature, colloqui e crescita professionale. Molte parole formano collocazioni fisse (apply for, cope with): imparale insieme al verbo.

ex: She has had a successful career in journalism.
Ha avuto una carriera di successo nel giornalismo.
words.note: Accento sulla seconda sillaba. Mai «carrier» (che significa «trasportatore, vettore»).

ex: I'm going to apply for a job at the council.
Farò domanda per un posto al comune.
words.note: Il nome è application. Non «apply to a job».

ex: You need a teaching qualification for this post.
Per questo posto serve un titolo di abilitazione all'insegnamento.
words.note: Si dice have a qualification. Un titolo di studio è degree o diploma.

ex: We interviewed six candidates yesterday.
Ieri abbiamo intervistato sei candidati.
He resigned after an argument with his boss.
Si è dimesso dopo una discussione con il capo.
words.note: Il nome è resignation. Pronuncia con /z/.

ex: She got a promotion after only a year.
Ha ottenuto una promozione dopo solo un anno.
words.note: Il verbo è be promoted. Non è la promozione commerciale (special offer).

ex: About fifty workers were made redundant last year.
L'anno scorso una cinquantina di lavoratori sono stati licenziati per esubero.
words.note: «Redundant» NON significa «ridondante» in questo senso. Se ti licenziano per un errore: be sacked / fired.

ex: My employer pays for my English course.
Il mio datore di lavoro mi paga il corso di inglese.
My workload has doubled since January.
Il mio carico di lavoro è raddoppiato da gennaio.
Could you give me a reference for my application?
Potresti scrivermi una referenza per la mia candidatura?
words.note: Si dice give / write a reference.

ex: How do you cope with so much stress?
Come fai a gestire così tanto stress?
The company is taking on ten new staff.
L'azienda sta assumendo dieci nuovi dipendenti.
words.note: Vale anche per «accettare un compito»: take on extra work.

ex: My main strength is working in a team.
Il mio punto di forza principale è lavorare in squadra.
Teaching can be tiring, but it is very rewarding.
Insegnare può essere stancante, ma è molto gratificante.

steps.s: She's very ambitious and wants to build a successful ___ in finance.
steps.why: «Career» = percorso professionale; «carrier» è un falso amico (vettore, corriere).

steps.s: My job is stressful, but I ___ with it by going for a run every evening.
steps.why: «Cope with» = riuscire a gestire una situazione difficile.

steps.q: Completa con una parola
steps.s: The firm is closing one of its offices, so thirty employees will be made ___ .
steps.sub: L'azienda chiude una sede, quindi trenta dipendenti saranno licenziati per esubero.

steps.s: After ten years in the same job, she decided to ___ and travel.
steps.why: Serve il verbo: resignation -> resign.

steps.s: You need a professional ___ to work as an accountant.
steps.why: Serve un nome: qualify -> qualification.

steps.q: Quale frase è corretta?
opts: I'm applying for the position of sales assistant.
I'm applying to the position of sales assistant.
I'm applying the position of sales assistant.
steps.why: Si dice apply for a job / position.

steps.q: Traduci in inglese
steps.text: Il mio punto di forza è risolvere i problemi.
answers: My main strength is solving problems
My strength is to solve problems
My main strength is problem solving
steps.why: Dopo is si usa di solito la forma in -ing.

lessons.title: Dalla sala al ruolo di responsabile
lessons.intro: Un articolo racconta la carriera di una donna che ha iniziato lavorando in un ristorante. Nota quante volte compare il present perfect e perché.

steps.title: From waitress to events manager
steps.text:
When Nadia Rahman left school at eighteen, she had no idea what she wanted to do. "I just knew I didn't want to go to university," she says. "I needed money, so I took the first job I found."

That job was in a busy restaurant in Manchester, and she has never regretted it. She has been working in the hospitality industry for fourteen years now, and in that time she has done almost every job there is: waitress, bar manager, even cook for a short period. "People think working in a restaurant isn't a real career," she says, "but I've learnt more about people than any course could teach me."

Her big break came six years ago, when the owner of the restaurant asked her to organise a large wedding. She had never planned anything like it, but she accepted the challenge. The event went so well that she was offered a position as events coordinator, and she has been organising conferences, parties and weddings ever since. Last spring she was promoted again, and she now manages a team of twelve people.

Has it been easy? Not always. For the last two years she has been studying part-time for a business qualification in the evenings, and she admits that she has often felt exhausted. "There have been moments when I wanted to give up," she says. "I've missed a lot of social events, and my friends have almost stopped inviting me!" However, she has just passed her first exams, and she says it has all been worthwhile.

Her advice to young people is simple. "Don't worry if you haven't decided on your career yet. Take opportunities when they come, say yes to challenges, and be honest about what you can't do. Since I started saying yes, my life has changed completely. I have been given chances I never imagined, and I haven't finished yet. Next year I'd like to open my own events company."

qs.q: Why did Nadia take her first job?
qs.why: «I needed money, so I took the first job I found.»

qs.q: Nadia has worked in hospitality for ___ years.
What changed her career six years ago?
opts: She moved to a new restaurant.
qs.why: «...the owner asked her to organise a large wedding... she was offered a position as events coordinator».
Non è andata all'università: studia part-time la sera per una qualifica.

qs.q: Nadia's parents wanted her to go to university.
qs.why: Il testo non parla dei genitori.

qs.q: What does Nadia say about her studies?
opts: They have been hard but worthwhile.
They have not helped her career.
qs.why: «...she has often felt exhausted... it has all been worthwhile».

opts: Accept challenges and be honest about your limits.
Decide your career as early as possible.
qs.why: «Take opportunities... say yes to challenges, and be honest about what you can't do».

qs.q: Nadia's plan for next year is to open her own ___ .
qs.why: «Next year I'd like to open my own events company.»

steps.q: Nel testo, «her big break» significa:
opts: l'occasione che ha cambiato la sua carriera

steps.q: Completa con una parola del testo
steps.s: There were moments when she wanted to give ___ .

steps.q: «She has often felt exhausted» significa che Nadia:

steps.s: She was ___ to manager after the conference went so well.
steps.why: «Be promoted» = ricevere una promozione di carriera.

lessons.title: Cambiare carriera a quarant'anni
lessons.intro: Un'intervista radiofonica con un ex contabile che oggi fa il falegname. Ascolta con attenzione i periodi di tempo: sono la chiave di molte risposte.

steps.title: A new career at forty
steps.it: Ascolta l'intervista e rispondi. Puoi riascoltarla e usare la velocità lenta.
lines: Welcome back to Work Matters. My guest today is Mark Dolan, who changed careers at forty. Mark, you were an accountant, weren't you?
That's right. I worked for a bank for sixteen years. I was good at it, but I wasn't happy.
Well, a trainee carpenter, really. I've been learning the job for about eighteen months.
How long have you been planning this?
Longer than I'd like to admit. I started dreaming about it five years ago, but I was afraid. I had a mortgage and two children.
So what finally changed your mind?
My father, actually. He retired last year, and he told me he had never done the work he really wanted. I didn't want to say the same thing at sixty-five.
Financially, yes. I've earned less than half my old salary since I left the bank. And I've made plenty of mistakes. Last month I cut a beautiful table leg an inch too short!
Not for a second. I've never felt so tired, and I've never felt so happy. My advice? Talk to people who have already done it, and save some money first.

qs.q: How long did Mark work at the bank?
How long has Mark been learning carpentry?
Why didn't Mark change career earlier?
Since he left the bank, Mark has earned less than ___ of his old salary.
What mistake did Mark make last month?
opts: He cut a table leg too short.
Speak to people who have changed career and save money.

steps.en: I've been learning the job for about eighteen months.
steps.it: Imparo il mestiere da circa diciotto mesi.

steps.en: I've earned less than half my old salary since I left the bank.
steps.it: Da quando ho lasciato la banca guadagno meno della metà del mio vecchio stipendio.

steps.en: I haven't decided yet, but I've been thinking about it for months.
steps.it: Non ho ancora deciso, ma ci penso da mesi.

lessons.title: Il colloquio di lavoro
lessons.intro: Le domande che quasi sempre vengono fatte in un colloquio e come rispondere in modo sicuro ma non arrogante. Impari anche a fare domande all'intervistatore in modo educato.

steps.title: Le domande tipiche e come rispondere
steps.body:
Domande che troverai quasi sempre:
- **Tell me about yourself.** = Mi parli di lei.
- **Why do you want this job?** / **Why are you leaving your current job?**
- **What are your strengths and weaknesses?**
- **How long have you been working in this field?**
- **Where do you see yourself in five years?**

Una struttura semplice per rispondere: **presente + passato recente + obiettivo**.
- **I'm currently working as...** (presente)
- **I've been doing this for... and I've learnt...** (present perfect)
- **I'd like to... / I'm looking for...** (obiettivo)

Per i punti deboli: non dire «I have no weaknesses». Meglio: **I used to find it hard to delegate, but I've been working on it.**
ex: I've been working as a nurse for six years.
Lavoro come infermiera da sei anni.
I'm looking for a new challenge.
Cerco una nuova sfida.

steps.title: Tono: educato, non troppo diretto
steps.body:
In un colloquio il tono conta quanto il contenuto. Confronta:
- troppo diretto: «How much will you pay me?» -> più educato: **Could you tell me a little about the salary and benefits?**
- troppo diretto: «I want this job.» -> **I'd be very interested in this position.**
- troppo vago: «I'm good at everything.» -> **I'd say my main strength is working under pressure.**

Al termine dell'intervista:
- **Do you have any questions for us?** -> **Yes, could you tell me more about the training?**
- **Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.**

**Errore tipico degli italiani**: «I have experience of 3 years» è un calco dall'italiano: si dice **I have three years' experience**. E «I'm available to start immediately» va benissimo.
ex: Could you tell me a little more about the role?
Potrebbe dirmi qualcosa di più sul ruolo?
I'd say my main weakness is that I'm a perfectionist.
Direi che il mio principale difetto è il perfezionismo.

steps.title: Il colloquio
steps.it: Scegli la risposta più adatta a un colloquio (Tu).
lines: Good morning. Please take a seat. So, tell me a little about yourself.

opts: I'm an administrative assistant, and I've been working in the insurance sector for five years. Recently I've been looking for more responsibility.
I am working in insurance since five years and I want more responsibility, so I am here.
I'm an administrative assistant. I don't have much to say about me.

lines: I see. Why are you leaving your current job?

opts: I've enjoyed my time there, but there isn't much room for progress, and I'd like to develop my skills.
My boss is terrible and the salary is too low, so I'm going away.
I am leaving because I am boring.

lines: Good. What would you say is your main strength?

opts: I'd say I'm very organised, and I stay calm when the workload gets heavy.
I'm better than my colleagues in everything.
I am very organised and I have a lot of qualities that you can't imagine.

steps.why: Nel primo scambio servono present perfect (for / since) per la durata e un tono positivo. Evita critiche al datore di lavoro e frasi esagerate.

steps.title: Alla fine del colloquio
lines: Well, that's all from me. Do you have any questions for us?

opts: Yes, I'd like to know a little more about the training for new staff, if that's possible.
Yes. How much money do I get every month?
No. I only want to know when I start.

lines: Of course. Everyone has a two-week induction, and then a mentor for six months.

opts: That sounds excellent. And could you tell me when you expect to make a decision?
Good. When do you tell me yes or no?

lines: We'll let you know by the end of next week.

opts: Thank you very much for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.
Thank you. I wait your answer.

pairs: Where do you see yourself in five years?
Dove si vede tra cinque anni?
I look forward to hearing from you.
Spero di avere presto vostre notizie.
Could you tell me more about the role?
Potrebbe dirmi di più sul ruolo?
I'd say my main strength is...
Direi che il mio punto di forza è...

steps.it: Lavoro nelle vendite da circa sei anni.
steps.en: I have been working in sales for about six years
I've been working as a nurse for six years.
steps.it: Lavoro come infermiera da sei anni.

steps.en: I'd say my main strength is working under pressure.
steps.it: Direi che il mio punto di forza è lavorare sotto pressione.

steps.en: Could you tell me a little more about the training?
steps.it: Potrebbe dirmi qualcosa in più sulla formazione?

steps.q: Answer the question: Tell me about yourself and your work experience.
steps.it: Rispondi come in un colloquio: presente (che cosa fai ora), passato recente (da quanto tempo, che cosa hai imparato), obiettivo (che cosa cerchi). Almeno 6 frasi.
hints: I've been doing this for... and I've learnt...
steps.model: I'm currently working as a project assistant for a software company in Turin. I've been doing this job for four years, and during that time I've learnt how to manage deadlines and work with clients. I've also been taking an evening course in project management for the last year. I'm very organised and I enjoy working in a team. Now I'm looking for a position with more responsibility, where I can use my skills and keep learning.

lessons.title: La lettera di candidatura
lessons.intro: Scriverai una breve lettera di candidatura formale: il tipo di testo che accompagna un CV. Poi parlerai di te come in un colloquio.

steps.title: Struttura di una lettera formale
steps.body:
- **Saluto**: Dear Ms Taylor, / Dear Sir or Madam, (se non conosci il nome)
- **Motivo**: I am writing to apply for the position of... advertised on...
- **Esperienza**: I have been working as... for... / I have experience of...
- **Qualità e motivazione**: I am hard-working, reliable and... / I would like to work for you because...
- **Chiusura**: I have attached my CV. / I would be happy to attend an interview. / I look forward to hearing from you.
- **Formula finale**: **Yours sincerely** (se conosci il nome) / **Yours faithfully** (con Sir or Madam), poi nome e cognome.

Stile formale: niente contrazioni, niente slang. Frasi complete e cortesi (I would be grateful if..., Thank you for considering my application).
ex: I am writing to apply for the position of receptionist.
Scrivo per candidarmi al posto di receptionist.
I look forward to hearing from you.
Spero di avere presto vostre notizie.

steps.s: Dear Sir or Madam, ... I look forward to hearing from you. Yours ___ ,
steps.why: Con «Dear Sir or Madam» (nome sconosciuto) si chiude con Yours faithfully.

steps.s: I have been working as a sales assistant ___ three years.
steps.why: Un periodo di tempo si introduce con «for».

steps.s: I want to apply to the job of receptionist that you advertised on your website.
answers: I want to apply for the job of receptionist that you advertised on your website
I want to apply for the job of receptionist advertised on your website
I am writing to apply for the job of receptionist that you advertised on your website
I am writing to apply for the job of receptionist advertised on your website
I would like to apply for the job of receptionist that you advertised on your website
I would like to apply for the job of receptionist advertised on your website
steps.why: Si dice «apply for», non «apply to». (Il resto della frase è già corretto.)

steps.s1: I started working at this company in 2020.
steps.why: Nella lettera, la durata si esprime con il present perfect continuous.

steps.q: You have seen this advertisement: 'Sales assistant wanted. Busy sports shop in the city centre. Good English essential. Experience in retail preferred. Apply in writing to Ms Taylor.' Write a letter of application. Say why you are writing, describe your experience, and explain why you would be a good candidate.
steps.it: Scrivi una lettera di candidatura formale (100-120 parole) a Ms Taylor: motivo della lettera, la tua esperienza (usa il present perfect con for/since) e perché saresti adatto.
checklist: Ho iniziato con Dear Ms Taylor e chiuso con Yours sincerely
Ho spiegato perché scrivo (I am writing to apply for...)
Ho usato il present perfect con for o since per la mia esperienza
Ho citato almeno due qualità o punti di forza
Ho usato uno stile formale, senza contrazioni
useful: I am writing to apply for...
I have been working as... for...
I look forward to hearing from you.
steps.model:
Dear Ms Taylor,

I am writing to apply for the position of sales assistant advertised in your shop window.

I have been working as a shop assistant at a sports shop in Verona for three years, and I have dealt with customers every day. I have also trained two new colleagues, so I know how to explain things clearly.

I am hard-working, reliable and good with people. I have studied English since I was twelve, and I have just passed the B1 exam. I would like to develop my career in a larger company.

I have attached my CV and I would be happy to attend an interview at any time.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,
Giulia Bianchi

steps.q: Why do you want this job? Why should we choose you?
steps.it: Rispondi come in un colloquio: perché vuoi questo lavoro e perché dovrebbero scegliere te (almeno 5 frasi).
hints: I'm very interested in this position because...
I'd be a good choice because...
steps.model: I'm very interested in this position because it would let me use my experience in customer service. I've been working with clients for five years, and I've learnt how to stay calm in difficult situations. My main strengths are communication and organisation. I'd be a good choice because I'm reliable, I learn quickly, and I really enjoy working in a team.

steps.q: Talk about your career so far and your plans.
steps.it: Racconta il tuo percorso finora (studi, lavori, da quanto tempo fai qualcosa) e che cosa vorresti fare in futuro.
hints: I studied... and then I started...
In five years I'd like to...
steps.model: I studied languages at university, and then I started working as a translator. I've been working freelance for three years, and I've learnt how to manage my own time. Recently I've been learning about marketing because I'd like to move into communications. In five years I'd like to be working for an international company, ideally in a team with people from different countries.

lessons.title: Test dell'unità 1
lessons.intro: Verifica senza aiuti: present perfect, for/since, how long, lessico del lavoro, un testo e un ascolto. Le correzioni le vedi alla fine.

steps.s: She ___ in marketing since she graduated.
How many emails ___ today?
Come on, I ___ for you since eight o'clock!
Marco left the company two years ___ .
